title: Exceptional coefficient and base-change compatibility square
statement: Let $A,B$ be finite commutative rings in universe $u+1$ and $\phi:A\to B$ a unital map. For schemes $X,Y,Y'$ in universe $u$ [def-pc-scheme], work in ordinary etale derived module categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and let $S_T$ denote derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be compactifiable [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $g:Y'\to Y$, and write $f',g'$ for the Cartesian projections [def-pc-base-change]. For $K\in D(Y_{et},A)$, use the canonical exceptional coefficient mate $c_{f,K}$ [def-per-exceptional-coefficient-maps], exceptional base-change map $\beta$ [def-asd-smooth-dualizing-base-change-arrows], and uniquely normalized scalar/pullback comparison $\chi:g^*S_Y\simeq S_{Y'}g^*$ [lem-pur-etale-scalar-mate-projection]. Define base-change compatibility to be the equality of the following two maps from $S_{X'}g'^*G_{f,A}K$ to $G_{f',B}g^*S_YK$: first apply $S_{X'}(\beta_{A,f,g,K})$, then $c_{f',g^*K}$, then $G_{f',B}(\chi_g^{-1}(K))$; alternatively apply $\chi_{g'}^{-1}(G_{f,A}K)$, then $g'^*(c_{f,K})$, then $\beta_{B,f,g,S_YK}$. This defines a proposition only and asserts neither that the square commutes nor that its arrows are isomorphisms.
